scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Both user LANs lost cross-AS connectivity this morning: pc1
(195.11.14.2) cannot reach pc2 (200.1.1.2) and pc2 cannot reach
pc1. Each PC still reaches its own gateway fine. Our NOC checked
router1: its inter-AS interface eth0 shows UP and its config is
unchanged. The partner operator (AS 2) says router2's logs show
the eBGP session dropping. Find what broke.

injection.action: administratively down the inter-AS interface (eth0) on router2

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router2 eth0 (193.10.11.2/24, the inter-AS
  interface toward router1)
Mechanism: router2's eth0 is DOWN, so the physical/L2 path between
  the two ASes is broken at router2's side. router2 immediately
  loses its 193.10.11.0/24 connected route and its BGP route to
  195.11.14.0/24 (nexthop interface gone), and its side of the
  eBGP session drops. Traffic from pc1 toward 200.1.1.0/24 is
  blackholed on the inter-AS segment (nothing listens at
  193.10.11.2 any more), so pc1<->pc2 fails in both directions.
  Note: router1's eth0 still shows UP (the far side of the virtual
  link keeps carrier), and router1 may briefly keep showing the
  session as Established until its hold timer expires -- the
  definitive evidence is router2's eth0 being DOWN.
Localization: router2
Root cause: inter-AS link down at router2 (eth0 administratively
  down)
Fix: `ip link set eth0 up` on router2
scenario.fix_spec:
Bring the inter-AS link back up: on router2 run `ip link set eth0 up`. The
eBGP session re-establishes, the inter-AS prefixes are re-exchanged, and pc1
reaches pc2 normally. router1 needs no change -- it was healthy the whole time.

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: the L2 inter-AS link on router2 (interface eth0) is down, breaking the eBGP peering and data plane between AS1 and AS2. 

Mechanism: With router2:eth0 down, router2 cannot ARP or pass traffic to 193.10.11.0/24, so its BGP session to 193.10.11.1 never establishes (Active state). Router1 briefly still shows the session Established and retains the 200.1.1.0/24 route due to the 180s BGP hold timer, but actual forwarding fails because ARP to 193.10.11.2 is unresolved, yielding “Destination Host Unreachable” from 195.11.14.1 during pc1→pc2 pings.

Localization: On router2, eth0 is DOWN at L2: ip link show dev eth0 reports state DOWN; ethtool for router2 eth0 shows “Link detected: no.” Router2’s routing table lacks any BGP-learned routes (only connected 200.1.1.0/24), and “show bgp summary” is Active. On router1, ARP for 193.10.11.2 is incomplete and pings to 193.10.11.2 fail; yet its BGP neighbor still appears Established with last read ~109s and hold time 180s, consistent with a dead link not yet timed out.

Root cause: router2’s inter-AS interface eth0 was taken down (administratively or due to link failure), severing the 193.10.11.0/24 peering network.

Corrective fix: Bring router2:eth0 back up (e.g., ip link set dev eth0 up) and verify L1/L2 (“ethtool ... link detected: yes”). Confirm BGP on both sides (show bgp summary should be Established) and ensure routes to 195.11.14.0/24 and 200.1.1.0/24 are present. Optionally tighten BGP timers or enable BFD for faster failure detection in the future.
